product: Product is liquefied natural gas plus regasified gas. Cheniere buys US natural gas, liquefies it at Sabine Pass (Louisiana) and Corpus Christi (Texas), charters vessels and sells LNG under long-term fixed-fee SPAs and IPM deals. Demand is global - Europe and Asia, 46 markets and regions (cheniere.com, read 2026-09-27).
demand: Volume-led with margin mix. Q2 2026 revenue rose 24 percent to 5.73B on 184 cargoes (plus 19 percent) and 672 TBtu (plus 22 percent); H1 1,360 TBtu (plus 17 percent) (8-K 2026-08-06). Management credits higher volumes and higher margin per MMBtu plus optimization. FY26 production forecast tightened up to 53-54 Mt.
pricing_power: Compression of the international-versus-Henry-Hub gas spread that drives IPM margins, plus US gas price spikes. Cheniere's IPM deals are marked to market, and Q1 2026 produced 5.4B of unfavorable non-cash derivative moves and a 3.50B net loss (8-K 2026-05-07). New global supply from Qatar and others compressing LNG prices is the second path.
competition: Not found: a dated Chinese or other low-cost substitute action specific to Cheniere in the last 90 days. Structurally, Russian and Central Asian pipeline gas and Qatari LNG are cheaper alternatives, but distance, shipping and Cheniere's fixed-fee US-Gulf non-FTA volumes make it a differentiated product (cheniere.com, read 2026-09-27).
market_strategy: CEO Jack Fusco, 2026-08-06 (SEC 8-K EX-99.1): 'we have once again raise[d] our full year 2026 Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA and Distributable Cash Flow guidance ranges. We look forward to delivering full year financial results within these further improved ranges.' On 2026-05-07 he promised 'accretive, brownfield growth at Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi.'
bull: Q2 2026 revenue rose 24% to 5.73B on 184 cargoes; FY26 EBITDA guidance raised twice to 7.90-8.40B; Train 6 complete and FERC added 5 mtpa (8-K 2026-08-06).
bear: Q1 2026 net loss 3.50B on 5.4B unfavorable IPM derivative marks; revenue fell 2.3% QoQ; SPL Expansion FID still pending FERC/DOE; 21-session momentum -5.5%.
falsifier: FY2026 Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA reported below the raised 7.90B floor, or any guidance cut, in the Q4 2026 8-K.
web_what_changed_30_90d: Last 30 days to 2026-09-27: no company press releases (news count 0); sell-side targets rose - Scotiabank 290 to 312 (2026-09-10), Goldman Sachs 305 (2026-09-11), Bernstein 283 (2026-09-22), Morgan Stanley 310 (2026-09-25), per stockanalysis.com. Last 90 days: Q2 2026 results, FY26 EBITDA guidance raised to 7.90-8.40B, Train 6 complete, FERC plus 5 mtpa (all 2026-08-06, SEC 8-K).
web_true_now_not_modelled: GAAP net income is dominated by non-cash IPM derivative mark-to-market: Q2 2026 net income 3.07B on about 1.4B favorable derivative moves (8-K 2026-08-06), while Q1 2026 was a 3.50B loss on 5.4B unfavorable moves (8-K 2026-05-07). Analysts track EBITDA and DCF, but the earnings optics and derivative swings may not be modelled. Guidance was raised twice in 2026.
web_demand_product: Product is liquefied natural gas plus regasified gas. Cheniere buys US natural gas, liquefies it at Sabine Pass (Louisiana) and Corpus Christi (Texas), charters vessels and sells LNG under long-term fixed-fee SPAs and IPM deals. Demand is global - Europe and Asia, 46 markets and regions (cheniere.com, read 2026-09-27).
web_price_volume_mix: Volume-led with margin mix. Q2 2026 revenue rose 24 percent to 5.73B on 184 cargoes (plus 19 percent) and 672 TBtu (plus 22 percent); H1 1,360 TBtu (plus 17 percent) (8-K 2026-08-06). Management credits higher volumes and higher margin per MMBtu plus optimization. FY26 production forecast tightened up to 53-54 Mt.
web_bottleneck: Company bottleneck is construction and permitting: Train 7 commissioning, CCL Trains 8 and 9, and pending FERC and DOE approvals for SPL Expansion and CCL Expansion, with FID not yet taken (8-K 2026-08-06). Cheniere relieves Europe and Asia gas-supply insecurity; the binding constraint is US Gulf Coast liquefaction capacity, not gas supply.
web_who_benefits_next: Second-order: Bechtel (EPC contractor for SPL Expansion Phase 1 under a May 2026 lump-sum contract and LNTP, 8-K 2026-08-06); US gas producers; LNG shipping firms; Gulf Coast pipelines; CQP unitholders. Also lower borrowing costs after the February 2026 Moody's upgrade (8-K 2026-05-07). Third-order: European and Asian utilities seeking supply diversity.
web_who_loses: Rival LNG exporters (Qatar, Australia, Canada, other US Gulf projects) lose share and pricing power; Russian pipeline gas into Europe loses market. Inference from Cheniere's stated 46-market reach and expansion plans (cheniere.com 2026-09-27; 8-K 2026-08-06). Buyers lose leverage as fixed-fee US volumes lock in, and US domestic gas users face export-driven price pressure.

We look forward to delivering full year financial results within these further improved ranges.' On 2026-05-07 he promised 'accretive, brownfield growth at Sabine Pass and Corpus Christi.'
web_did_they_deliver: Yes so far. FY26 guidance raised twice: 2026-05-07 (EBITDA 6.75-7.25B to 7.25-7.75B) and 2026-08-06 (7.25-7.75B to 7.90-8.40B) (SEC 8-Ks). Promised train milestones met - Train 5 substantial completion March 2026 and Train 6 June 2026. Dividends of 0.555 per quarter paid; 1.1B buybacks in H1 2026.
web_what_would_falsify: Observable falsifiers: FY2026 Consolidated Adjusted EBITDA below the raised 7.90B floor or any guidance cut (8-K 2026-08-06); Train 7 first LNG slipping beyond fall 2026; SPL Expansion FID not taken in 2026 or FERC/DOE denial; consensus mean target (309.95, 22 analysts, stockanalysis.com 2026-09-25) falling toward the 268.54 close.
